concept_summary: Hodai Restaurant: a beer-and-wine restaurant at 2183 Mission St in the Mission Street NCT district, proposing limited cooking, five employees and tenant improvements.

lines.text: The concept is looked up as a Restaurant (Planning Code § 102).
Zoning district NCT-MISSION: a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 754, in force since before 2022-01-01).

NCT-MISSION: the table caps the eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) in the district at 167, and a new one is not permitted if it would take the total above that (Table 754 Note 7, in force since before 2022-01-01). The records do not show how many there are.

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: Any proposed Restaurant in the sub-area east of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street needs Conditional Use, with or without alcohol. Zoning district NCT-MISSION lies inside that sub-area: a conditional use (Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol; its licence may be transferred from inside or from outside the district. The district adds no Conditional Use for the licence itself (but see subsection (f)(1) for the Restaurant use in the sub-area). This rule asks for nothing here (Planning Code § 249.60(b)(1)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: The § 202.2 operating conditions apply to every liquor establishment in the district; new, relocated or expanded ones, and any with a licence referred to Planning by ABC, must also provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% and keep 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 249.60(d), in force since before 2022-01-01).
Zoning district NCT-MISSION has no hours of operation control on file (Planning Code § 754, in force since before 2022-01-01), so this trigger does not apply.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full conditional use authorization to legalize a restaurant (Bissap Baobab) at 3372 19th St (192 m, NCT-MISSION zoning) that filed Sept 2018 and was approved March 2019 with 14 conditions. This is a use-decision hearing, the type 2183 Mission would face.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The only recent CUA for a restaurant in NCT-MISSION within 1,000 ft was approved with conditions but took six months from filing to approval. Key conditions included hours limited to Tues–Sun 11 a.m.–1:45 a.m., soundproofing, odor control, sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, and a community liaison requirement. Extended late-night hours (until 1:45 a.m.) were permitted.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to establish a new restaurant in a vacant commercial space at 600 South Van Ness (191 m, UMU zoning, Mission area), filed March 2018, approved Aug 2018 (5.5 months). comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Change-of-use CUA for a new restaurant in the Mission area was approved without extracted conditions within 5.5 months. UMU zoning treated restaurants more favorably than NCT-MISSION, but the case shows Planning approved new restaurant concepts during the Mission Interim Controls period.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: DPH referral for a continuation restaurant use at 3382 18th St (18 m away, NCT-MISSION zoning, essentially next door), approved Jan 2021 citing Planning Code §§ 754 and 249.60. This is the closest comparable geographically.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a restaurant continuation at the property immediately adjacent (18 m) under § 754 (NCT-MISSION restaurant rules) and § 249.60 (Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD rules). Agency referrals for continuations are routinely approved; a change of use triggers a conditional use hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving a Limited Restaurant (Ramenwell) at 3378 18th St (31 m, NCT-MISSION) as an existing permitted use under § 754 and the Mission Alcohol SUD rules (§§ 781.8 and 249.60), approved Aug 2018.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a limited restaurant very close by (31 m) within the Mission Alcohol SUD, citing both the NCT-MISSION district rules (§ 754) and the Special Use District overlay (§§ 781.8, 249.60). Limited restaurants face fewer hurdles than full restaurants, but the case confirms the dual-layer review within the SUD.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 41 ABC referral at 3378 18th St (31 m, NCT-MISSION) for a continuation of an existing restaurant use, approved April 2018. Same concept (restaurant with beer/wine) at nearly the same location.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 41 license for a restaurant continuation 31 m away as an agency referral in three weeks. Continuations are fast-tracked; a new restaurant filing as a change of use will face the full conditional use process with a Commission hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 47 (full-liquor) ABC referral for a restaurant at 2293 Mission St (186 m, NCT-MISSION), approved Sept 2020 as a continuation under § 754. Illustrates how alcohol licenses are handled within the district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 47 full-bar license for an existing restaurant 186 m away under § 754 as an agency referral. Full-liquor licenses are permitted for restaurants in the Mission Alcohol SUD if the restaurant operates as a Bona Fide Eating Place; the concept's Type 41 is less restrictive.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health department referral for a full-service restaurant at 2152 Mission St (63 m, NCT-MISSION), approved Nov 2018 (filed April 2017) as a continuation under §§ 790.92 and 712.42. This referral took 19 months, unusually long for an agency matter.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A restaurant continuation 63 m away was approved but took 19 months from filing to approval—an outlier timeline for an agency referral, suggesting administrative delays or incomplete submissions. Highlights the importance of complete plan sets and proactive coordination with all referral departments.

filing_playbook.action: Request a written answer from SF Planning on the current count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION against the 167 cap.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Write to the Planning Department's Zoning Information counter or file a Letter of Determination request, stating: 'We are evaluating a restaurant concept at 2183 Mission St (Parcel 3575/032, NCT-MISSION zoning). Planning Code § 754 Table 754 Note 7 caps eating and drinking uses in the district at 167. We request confirmation of the current count of Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars in the NCT-MISSION district, and whether a new Restaurant at this address would exceed the cap.' This determines whether the pathway is conditional use or not permitted.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain a federal EIN, then register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to receive a Business Account Number.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation online through the Secretary of State's bizfile portal. Apply for the EIN online at irs.gov (free, issued immediately). Register the business at sftreasurer.org/business within 30 days; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (minimum $55 plus $4 state fee for a new business).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Complete the health permit application and schedule the DPH final inspection; obtain RBS and food handler certifications for all staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply for the Health Permit to Operate online with the BAN and LIN. Pay the $470 application fee (includes the initial inspection). Ensure at least one owner or employee has passed an ANSI-accredited food safety manager exam (ServSafe, Prometric, etc., $100–$250, valid 5 years). All employees who handle food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire ($7–$15 online, 2-hour course). All alcohol servers and their managers must complete ABC RBS training within 60 days of hire ($3 ABC portal registration plus $10–$25 course). Schedule the final DPH inspection; the inspector confirms the facility matches the approved plans and all equipment is in place. The permit is issued after the inspection passes.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and government cost of $6,500–$22,000 cover the Conditional Use Authorization, health permit to operate, and building permit with change of use when those approvals are granted. The range reflects: CUA hearing scheduling (120–180 days from filing to approval, based on the 2018–2019 comparables at 192 m and cases within 1,000 ft that took 6 months), building permit plan review and inspections (14–120 days depending on plan completeness and whether a change of occupancy is confirmed), and DPH plan check and inspections (21–60 days). ABC Type 41 licence processing (60–120 days per the catalog) is not included in the day or cost totals because the alcohol licence row's status is insufficient information; if a new Type 41 is required and the census tract's undue concentration triggers a Public Convenience or Necessity finding, add 1–3 months and the ABC $1,000–$1,600 licence fee. Costs shown are government permit and inspection fees only: CUA application approximately $3,150, DPH plan check $828–$2,207 (depending on scope), health permit application $470 (plus $0 annual licence fee for restaurants in FY2026–27), building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction valuation), business registration $55–$95 (for a new small business), entity formation $70–$150, and miscellaneous items (FOG, sign permit, seller's permit, EDD, workers' comp setup) $0–$2,000. The timeline does not account for a denial or a withdrawal; it is a time to approval. Construction, architecture, legal, and licence broker fees are not government costs and are not included.

records_summary: 2183 Mission St sits in the Mission Street NCT zoning district and inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. The pathway analysis shows that a Restaurant here is a conditional use, and this is a change of use since the site history shows the space was most recently operated as a fast-food restaurant (legal nonconforming use, last approved 2010). The block is extremely dense: 26 food & drink businesses within 500 ft, 5 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, and 48 ABC licenses within 1,000 ft. Planning records show only 6 dated use decisions in the NCT-MISSION district within 1,000 ft over the last 5 years (1 approved, 3 approved with conditions, 2 withdrawn), far too few to calculate an approval rate, but all four approvals involved restaurants or eating places.
